lines: אזא 28 אזל
in that place, there, kindred with זֶה,
Arab. إِنْ ecce ! Then
1. Part. demonstr. of time, at that time,
then, Chald. אֱדַיִן. Spoken: a) Of time
past, Arab. إِنْ, Gen. 12, 6. Josh. 10, 12.
14, 11. With præt. 1 K. 8, 12. 2 Chr.
6, 1. 8, 12. 17; also with fut. in præter
sense, Josh. l. c. Ex. 15, 1. Deut. 4, 41.
Comp. Lehrg. p. 773. b) Of a future
time, then, thereupon, after that; with
fut. in fut. sense, Ps. 96, 12 אָז יְרַנְּנוּ then
shall they rejoice. Sometimes also with
præt. in a future sense, where a future
precedes, Judg. 5, 11. Ex. 15, 15.
2. Part. illat. then, for thence, there-
fore, on that account, Jer. 22, 15. Ps.
3. With pref. מֵאָז and מִן־אָז, pr. from
that time, from then ; hence a) Adv.
from ancient times, of old, long since,
48, 3. 5. 7. b) Prep. and Conj. from the
time, from when, since, Fr. depuis, dès-
lors, c. inf. Ex. 4, 10 מֵאָז דַּבֶּרְךָ since
thou hast spoken. Josh. 14, 10. With
subst. Ruth 2, 7 מֵאָז הַבֹּקֶר from the time
of morning, since morning. Ps. 76, 8
מֵאָז אַפֶּךָ from the time of thy anger, i. e.
when once thou art angry. As Conj.
with a finite verb, pr. for מֵאָז אֲשֶׁר, from
the time that, since, Ex. 5, 23 מֵאָז בָּאתִי
אֶל פַּרְעֹה since I came unto Pharaoh.
Note. Fuller forms from אָז are אֲזַי
q. v. and Chald. אֱדַיִן. The latter seems
to have come (by softening the letters)
from הֵידֵין, הָדֵין, here, also there; so
that its ending appears to be plural,
while in fact it is not so; comp. עֲדַיִן for
עַד־הֵן. See, for these particles and their
etymology, Hupfeld in Zeitschr. f. d.
Kunde des Morgenl. II. p. 434.
* אֲזָא and אֲזָה Chald. to light, to
kindle; comp. Arab. أَزَّ to be hot, to light
a fire. Part. pass. אֵזֵה by Syriasm for
אֲזֵה Dan. 3, 22; inf. מֵזֵא for מֵאזֵא, c.
suff. מֵזְיֵהּ 3, 19.
* אָזַב obsol. root, whence אֵזוֹב q. v.
אֶזְבַּי pr. n. m. Ezbai, 1 Chr. 11, 37.
* אֲזַד Chald. i. q. אֲזַל to go away, to
depart. For the interchange of d and
l, comp. δάκρυον, lacryma, and see under
lett. ל no. 2.  Hence Dan. 2, 5. 8 מִלְּתָא
מִנִּי אַזְדָּא the word has gone out from me,
i. e. what I have said is ratified and can-
not be recalled ; comp. 9, 23. Is. 45, 23.
The Heb. intpp. as Saadias and Tanchum
of Jerus. have long ago well compared
the Talmudic phrase אזדא לטעמיה abiit
in sententiam suam, i. e. to follow one's
opinion.  As to the grammatical form,
אַזְדָּא is part. fem. from masc. אָזֵד, after
the form קָטֵל, אָזֵל.
אֵזוֹב m. (by Syriasm for אֱזוֹב ,) ὕσσω-
πος, hyssop, much used by the Hebrews
in their sacred purifications and sprink-
Ps. 51, 9. 1 K. 5, 13.—Like the names
of many other oriental plants, that of
hyssop also seems to have come to the
Greeks from the oriental languages.
Under this name the Hebrews appear to
have comprised not only the common
hyssop of the shops, but also other aro-
matic plants, espec. mint, wild marjoram,
etc.—Some derive it from אָזַב, which
they regard as i. q. زَبَّ to be hairy,
shaggy ; but the plants above named
hardly admit this epithet.
אֵזוֹר m. by Syriasm for אֵזוֹר. R.
אָזַר.
1. a girdle, belt, Is. 5, 27. Jer. 13, 1 sq.
2. a band, bond, chain, Job 12, 18.
Vulg. funis.
אֲזַי i. q. אָז, adv. at that time, then,
thereupon, Ps. 124, 3. 4. 5. Similar is
Chald. אֱדַיִן. See in אָז, note.
אַזְכָּרָה f. (verbal of Hiph. from r. זָכַר
in the sense of sacrificing Is. 66, 3 ; comp.
Hiph. no. 1. b,) a memorial, a remem-
brance-offering, Sept. μνημόσυνον, Vulg.
memoriale. This name was given to
that portion of the vegetable oblation
(מִנְחָה) which was burnt with frankin-
cense upon the altar; the sweet odour
of which ascending to heaven, was sup-
posed to commend the person sacrificing
to the remembrance and favour of God.
Lev. 24, 7 the frankincense sprinkled
upon the shew-bread, is also called
אַזְכָּרָה.
* אָזַל fut. יֵאזַל, whence תֵּזְלִי for
